Why XTOM exists

We build because real problems can't wait. We share because curiosity should never cost a thing. That's why XTOM exists.

Vision

A world where anyone, anywhere, can understand how technology works and use it to build something of their own.

Mission

Design practical engineering, software and learning tools for real life, and publish what we learn openly, without a paywall.

Engineering solutions

Mechanical and ocean engineering for concrete problems: concepts, CAD, simulation and working prototypes.

Open learning

Free courses, guides and tools, from German for daily life to how a ship stays afloat.

Everyday apps

Small, carefully made apps that save time and effort. Achso! and Canopy are the first two.

Fields we work in

Seven areas where engineering meets daily life, from the open sea to your desk. Each one is a home for future XTOM projects and free courses.

Advanced ship design

Efficient hulls, wind-assisted propulsion and CFD-driven optimization for cleaner shipping.

Underwater technology

ROVs, ocean sensors and hull design for working safely below the surface.

Robotics

Arms, grippers and control systems that take over repetitive or risky work.

Aerospace technology

Lighter, stronger airframes and wings shaped by aerodynamics, for aircraft and UAVs.

Mechanical design

From first sketch to CAD, tolerances and a part that actually fits.

3D printing

Rapid prototypes and printable spare parts that anyone can make at home.

Nature-inspired technology

Fins, shells and leaves as blueprints for quieter, more efficient machines.

Projects

Two mobile apps in testing and a seakeeping program in active research use.

Achso!German for real life

Testing on Android and iPhone

Learn the German you actually need, from the bakery to the Bürgeramt: lessons, speaking practice, games and everyday slang, set in landscapes from across Germany.

58units, A1 to B2
1,389words and phrases
24everyday dialogues

CanopyWallpapers made by code

Version 1.3.0 for Android

A wallpaper app that renders 3D scenes right on the phone, changes your wallpaper on a schedule and hides a few playful secrets for curious people.

4K3D renders on the phone
5free photo sources
Livewallpaper mode
Download Canopy APK

Version 1.3.0, 620 KB, for Android 8.0 or newer. The first time, your phone asks you to allow installs from your browser.

Xtom M.2

XTOM M.2Seakeeping for ships and multihulls

Version 2.10 for Windows

A desktop program that runs the whole seakeeping chain of monohulls, catamarans and trimarans in one place: hull mesh, stability, WAMIT or Capytaine hydrodynamics, damping, sea states, motions and operability.

3hull types
6degrees of freedom
2solvers, WAMIT and Capytaine
Ask about XTOM M.2

Built for ship research at the University of Rostock. Write to XTOM for a demo or access.

Past work

Engineering projects from Muthair's studies and research, from a 3D printer built in-house to a 15 MW floating wind turbine.

2025Research paper

Lattice propeller

A bio-inspired lattice inside a propeller blade: lighter, stiffer and made for metal 3D printing.

2025Offshore energy

Floating wind, 15 MW

Structure and hydrodynamics of a semi-submersible floating offshore wind turbine.

2025Ship design

Electric ferry

Hull form, structural analysis and optimization of a battery-electric passenger ferry.

2025Marine research

Underwater sensor float

A low-cost, multi-sensor float that dives to collect underwater data such as temperature, current velocity and pressure. Designed, built and sea-tested.

2022 to 2023Research paper

Low-cost robotic arm

A topology-optimized, fully 3D-printed robotic arm built at a fraction of the usual cost. Computer vision spots faulty parts and sorts them out.

2021Product development

Custom 3D printer

An industrial 3D printer designed and built in-house, cutting manufacturing cost by up to 35%.

Knowledge without a paywall

Learning on XTOM is free. Not a trial, not a light version: the full lessons, guides and tools, for anyone who wants to learn.

€9.99 / month €0
  • No subscriptions or paid tiers for learning, now or later.
  • Designs, drawings and code shared openly wherever we can.
  • Plain-language explanations, from first principles to advanced topics.

Meet the founder

I'm Muthair, a mechanical and ocean engineer. I love mechanical design, naval and ocean technology, robotics and aerospace.

I started XTOM to turn that curiosity into things people can use: everyday apps, engineering solutions for real problems, and free learning for anyone who wants it. Technology and knowledge shouldn't sit behind a subscription.
